incentives.title: Targets and bonuses
incentives.subtitle: Your bonus rules, the month-end calculations and their approval.
incentives.targetsSubtitle: One target per seller or per team. Leave empty for none.
incentives.newPlanHelp: A plan groups the bonus rules. It stays a draft until you activate it.
incentives.computeHelp: The calculation is a preview: redo it as often as needed before approving it.
incentives.plansEmpty: Create a plan, add its rules, then activate it.
incentives.rulesCount: {count, plural, =0 {no rule} one {# rule} other {# rules}}
incentives.draftHelp: Draft: add or change rules, then activate the plan.
incentives.activeHelp: Active plan: it can no longer be edited. To change a rule, create a new version.
incentives.archivedHelp: Archived plan: no longer used in calculations.
incentives.noRules: No rule yet. Add one to activate the plan.
incentives.newVersionHelp: The new version copies the current rules. It applies from the month you pick; the old one ends the day before.

typeHelp.FIXED_ON_TARGET: A fixed amount once a percentage of the target is reached.
typeHelp.TIERS: An amount or a rate depending on the target tier reached.
typeHelp.COMMISSION: A percentage of the figure, or only of what exceeds the target.
typeHelp.PER_UNIT: An amount for each unit sold of a brand, a category or a product.
typeHelp.MANAGER_OVERRIDE: For a supervisor: a percentage of the whole team’s figure, or an amount when the team reaches its target.

modeHelp.HIGHEST_REACHED: Only the highest tier reached pays.
modeHelp.PROGRESSIVE: Each tier reached pays its share, like brackets.

incentives.overrideAmount: an amount if the team reaches its target
incentives.gatesHelp: All must be met, or the rule pays nothing (e.g. collection rate ≥ 70 %).
incentives.exampleInvalid: Fill in “{field}” to see the example.
incentives.exampleNeedsNumbers: Type numbers to see the example.
incentives.outcomeGATE_FAILED: A condition is not met: nothing is paid.

incentives.noSellers: No seller yet. Invite your sellers from Settings › Users.

importFiles.title: Import files
importFiles.subtitle: One file per container: its receipts, its costs and the landed cost.
importFiles.emptyDescription: Create a file for a container, then attach its goods receipts and costs.
importFiles.openNotice: Open file: the goods of its receipts are in transit and cannot be sold yet. They enter stock, at the landed cost, when you close the file.
importFiles.closedNotice: File closed on {date}: the goods are in stock at the landed cost. A cost that arrives later is added as a late cost.
importFiles.attachBody: Only a receipt still in draft can join the file.
importFiles.detach: Remove the receipt from the file
importFiles.noPurchases: No receipts yet. Create the supplier's receipt from this file.
importFiles.costBody: Freight, customs, forwarder… A cost owed to a supplier is posted to its account right away.
importFiles.lateCostBody: The file is closed: this cost goes into the average cost of the units still in stock; the part for units already sold shows as cost variance. Past sales do not change.
importFiles.costSupplierHint: Forwarder or carrier: the amount is posted to its account.
importFiles.costTvaHint: Recoverable if you are VAT-registered: it then stays out of the landed cost.
importFiles.manualSplitHint: The sum must equal the amount to allocate. Total entered:
importFiles.previewHint: Preview: nothing is saved before closing.
importFiles.closeBody: The goods enter stock at the computed landed cost and the average cost is updated. A closed file cannot be cancelled: corrections go through a return, an adjustment or a late cost.
